expectedCard.summaryZh: 都柏林摄影工作室的背景布管理员，修补、上色、编目上百张背景。业余痴迷手写字体，一个字母的尾巴能磨一晚上；周日清早沿运河轮滑，三年了单脚还晃也不在意。她对小进展极有耐心，却听不得五年规划式的大话，一句'周四你打算做什么'就能把人问住。朋友考过驾照她郑重其事送卡庆祝，自己的成果却总一句'还没到能看的程度'带过。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums hard on the cafe window. At the next table, a woman slides a small practice page away from her cup, where the same letter sits written in rows.
beats.chinese: 雨点重重敲在咖啡馆窗上。邻桌的女人把一小页练习纸从杯子边挪开，纸上同一个字母写了一遍又一遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Listen to that. It's been hammering since I sat down. This tail has taken longer than the weather forecast, at this rate.
beats.chinese: 听那声音。我坐下起它就一直砸。照这速度，这条尾巴花的时间比天气预报还久。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the page with a pen cap, then glances over at the window, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 她用笔帽敲敲纸页，然后不紧不慢地瞥了一眼窗外。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm Aoife, by the way. Only reason I'm not out in it is the ink. Rain and a nib don't mix.
beats.chinese: 对了，我叫Aoife。我没出去就是因为在用墨水。雨和笔尖合不来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thirty-odd of these tails now. One of them came out decent. I'm not telling which.
beats.chinese: 这些尾巴写了三十多个了。有一个写得不错。我不说是哪个。

choices.english: Ask which one she's most satisfied with.
choices.chinese: 问她哪一个最满意。

choices.english: Ask whether practising the same letter doesn't get boring.
choices.chinese: 问练同一个字母会不会无聊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, none of them. Not fit to show yet. That's my rule — you don't put a half-cooked thing on the table.
beats.chinese: 啊，都不行。还没到能看的程度。这是我的规矩——半生不熟的东西不上桌。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She says it lightly, then turns the page towards herself and studies the rows properly, pen cap against her lip.
beats.chinese: 她轻描淡写地说完，把纸页转向自己，认真打量那几行，笔帽抵着嘴唇。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Though... row three, that one. The curve sits better than the others. It doesn't fight the downstroke.
beats.chinese: 不过……第三行那个。弧度比别的顺。它不跟竖笔较劲。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I did that one after the fourth coffee. Make of that what you will.
beats.chinese: 那是我第四杯咖啡之后写的。你自己琢磨吧。

choices.english: Ask her to compare just the first one and that last good one.
choices.chinese: 请她只比较最早的一个和最后那个好的。

choices.english: Say she doesn't need to show private practice pages.
choices.chinese: 表示她不必展示私人练习。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No, it doesn't bore me. That's the thing — small changes you can actually see.
beats.chinese: 不会，不无聊。妙就妙在这儿——小变化是看得见的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She draws a fresh row of the letter, slower this time, the nib scratching under the rain noise.
beats.chinese: 她重新写了一行这个字母，这次更慢，笔尖的沙沙声混在雨声里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This morning the loop closed too early. Now it doesn't. That's a whole day's work, and I can point at it.
beats.chinese: 早上那个圈收得太早。现在不会了。这就是一整天的活儿，我还能指给你看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Talk about who you'll be in five years — sure, who could argue with that? Nothing to check it against.
beats.chinese: 谈五年后你会成为谁——那种话谁都没法反驳？因为没东西可以对证。

choices.english: Ask what specifically she wants to practise next.
choices.chinese: 问她下次具体想练什么。

choices.english: Say you prefer having a big goal first.
choices.chinese: 说自己更喜欢先定个大目标。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lines the two rows side by side and holds the page up against the grey window light.
beats.chinese: 她把两行并排放好，把纸举到窗前灰蒙蒙的光下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. The first one, the curve dips before it lifts — like it lost nerve halfway. The last one commits all the way through.
beats.chinese: 好。第一个，弧线在扬起前先沉了下去——像中途没了胆气。最后那个一路到底。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps each with the pen cap, then pauses, looking at the page a moment longer than necessary.
beats.chinese: 她用笔帽逐一敲了敲，然后停住，盯着纸页看了一会儿，比必要的久一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Three months on this alphabet. That's the first time I've seen the difference with my own eyes, laid out like that.
beats.chinese: 这个字母表我练了三个月。这是我头一回亲眼看出差别，摆得这么明白。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All right. There's a bit of progress there. A small one — but I'll say it, since you made me measure it.
beats.chinese: 好吧。那儿是有一点进展。很小的一点——但我认了，是你逼我量出来的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the page in half, tucks it into a worn notebook, and gives the window a last look at the rain.
beats.chinese: 她把纸页对折，塞进一本磨旧的本子，最后看了一眼窗外的雨。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's decent of you. Most people grab at the page before you've said the word 'no'.
beats.chinese: 你这样挺好。大多数人话没说完就去抢着看纸了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She closes the notebook anyway and squares it on the table, keeping a thumb on the cover.
beats.chinese: 她还是合上了本子，在桌上摆正，拇指按在封面上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not precious, mind. I just don't count it finished. When it is, you'll get the whole alphabet, ink smudges and all.
beats.chinese: 倒也不是多金贵。只是我觉得它还没完成。等完成了，整本字母表都给你看，墨渍也算。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a friend of mine passed her driving test — I got her a card the size of a dinner plate. When mine's done, it'll get the same treatment. Not before.
beats.chinese: 我有个朋友考过了驾照——我给她买了张餐盘那么大的贺卡。等我的弄完了，也照这个规格办。在那之前免谈。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts her cup, nods at the rain still sliding down the glass, and settles back comfortably.
beats.chinese: 她端起杯子，朝还在玻璃上滑落的雨点点头，舒服地靠了回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Next? The join. Where the tail meets the next letter. I've been dodging it for two weeks.
beats.chinese: 下次？连接处。尾巴和下一个字母相接的地方。我躲了它两个星期。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She writes one letter, then a second, stopping the nib exactly where the two would meet.
beats.chinese: 她写了一个字母，又写第二个，笔尖在两者相接的位置停住。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See — alone, they're fine. Joined, the tail goes stiff. Same letter, same pen, different job.
beats.chinese: 看——分开写都好。一连起来，尾巴就僵了。同一个字母，同一支笔，干的活儿不一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So that's Thursday. Just the join, over and over, until it stops being stiff. I'm not promising it'll be pretty by the weekend.
beats.chinese: 所以周四就干这个。就练连接处，一遍一遍，直到它不僵为止。我可不许诺周末之前会好看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes that in without flinching, turning her cup a slow half-circle on the saucer.
beats.chinese: 她不动声色地听着，把杯子在碟子上慢慢转了半圈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Some people need the mountain in front of them or they won't take the first step. I'm just not built that way.
beats.chinese: 也行。有些人眼前得有座山才肯迈第一步。我只是天生不是那样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've seen grand plans go past my desk at the studio for eleven years. The ones that got finished were always the small, dull, daily ones.
beats.chinese: 十一年里，多少宏大的计划从我工作室桌前经过。最后做完的，总是那些又小又闷、每天做一点的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She adds one more letter to the row, then caps the pen and takes a proper drink of her coffee.
beats.chinese: 她在那行字上又添了一个字母，然后盖上笔，好好喝了一口咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway — different habits, same rain. As long as yours keeps you indoors out of this, it's doing its job.
beats.chinese: 总之——习惯不同，雨是同一场。只要它让你躲进屋里别淋着，它就尽到职责了。

beats.chinese: 雨又打在咖啡馆玻璃上。Aoife在包里翻找，掏出一个磨旧的轮滑护腕——紧紧裹着一个笔盒。

beats.speaker: npc

beats.chinese: 哎呀，瞧瞧。早上拿错了东西，就拿它来装笔了。今天保护的是字，不是手腕。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She unwinds it, shakes off a stray ink cap, and tucks both back into the bag, unbothered.
beats.chinese: 她把它解开，抖出一枚笔帽，把两样都收回包里，毫不在意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't worry, I'm not skating in this. Wet canal path — that's how wrists actually get ruined.
beats.chinese: 别担心，这种天我不轮滑。湿滑的运河步道——手腕才是那么弄坏的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The alphabet's coming along, slow as ever. When there's a whole row worth showing, you'll see it — not a page before.
beats.chinese: 字母表还在磨，照旧慢。等有值得看的一整行，你就能看到——之前一页也免谈。

beats.chinese: 不会，不无聊。妙就妙在这儿——小变化是看得见的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She draws a fresh row of the letter, slower this time, the nib scratching under the rain noise.
beats.chinese: 她重新写了一行这个字母，这次更慢，笔尖的沙沙声混在雨声里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This morning the loop closed too early. Now it doesn't. That's a whole day's work, and I can point at it.
beats.chinese: 早上那个圈收得太早。现在不会了。这就是一整天的活儿，我还能指给你看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Talk about who you'll be in five years — sure, who could argue with that? Nothing to check it against.
beats.chinese: 谈五年后你会成为谁——那种话谁都没法反驳？因为没东西可以对证。

choices.english: Ask what specifically she wants to practise next.
choices.chinese: 问她下次具体想练什么。

choices.english: Say you prefer having a big goal first.
choices.chinese: 说自己更喜欢先定个大目标。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lines the two rows side by side and holds the page up against the grey window light.
beats.chinese: 她把两行并排放好，把纸举到窗前灰蒙蒙的光下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. The first one, the curve dips before it lifts — like it lost nerve halfway. The last one commits all the way through.
beats.chinese: 好。第一个，弧线在扬起前先沉了下去——像中途没了胆气。最后那个一路到底。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps each with the pen cap, then pauses, looking at the page a moment longer than necessary.
beats.chinese: 她用笔帽逐一敲了敲，然后停住，盯着纸页看了一会儿，比必要的久一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Three months on this alphabet. That's the first time I've seen the difference with my own eyes, laid out like that.
beats.chinese: 这个字母表我练了三个月。这是我头一回亲眼看出差别，摆得这么明白。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All right. There's a bit of progress there. A small one — but I'll say it, since you made me measure it.
beats.chinese: 好吧。那儿是有一点进展。很小的一点——但我认了，是你逼我量出来的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the page in half, tucks it into a worn notebook, and gives the window a last look at the rain.
beats.chinese: 她把纸页对折，塞进一本磨旧的本子，最后看了一眼窗外的雨。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's decent of you. Most people grab at the page before you've said the word 'no'.
beats.chinese: 你这样挺好。大多数人话没说完就去抢着看纸了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She closes the notebook anyway and squares it on the table, keeping a thumb on the cover.
beats.chinese: 她还是合上了本子，在桌上摆正，拇指按在封面上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not precious, mind. I just don't count it finished. When it is, you'll get the whole alphabet, ink smudges and all.
beats.chinese: 倒也不是多金贵。只是我觉得它还没完成。等完成了，整本字母表都给你看，墨渍也算。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a friend of mine passed her driving test — I got her a card the size of a dinner plate. When mine's done, it'll get the same treatment. Not before.
beats.chinese: 我有个朋友考过了驾照——我给她买了张餐盘那么大的贺卡。等我的弄完了，也照这个规格办。在那之前免谈。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts her cup, nods at the rain still sliding down the glass, and settles back comfortably.
beats.chinese: 她端起杯子，朝还在玻璃上滑落的雨点点头，舒服地靠了回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Next? The join. Where the tail meets the next letter. I've been dodging it for two weeks.
beats.chinese: 下次？连接处。尾巴和下一个字母相接的地方。我躲了它两个星期。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She writes one letter, then a second, stopping the nib exactly where the two would meet.
beats.chinese: 她写了一个字母，又写第二个，笔尖在两者相接的位置停住。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See — alone, they're fine. Joined, the tail goes stiff. Same letter, same pen, different job.
beats.chinese: 看——分开写都好。一连起来，尾巴就僵了。同一个字母，同一支笔，干的活儿不一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So that's Thursday. Just the join, over and over, until it stops being stiff. I'm not promising it'll be pretty by the weekend.
beats.chinese: 所以周四就干这个。就练连接处，一遍一遍，直到它不僵为止。我可不许诺周末之前会好看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes that in without flinching, turning her cup a slow half-circle on the saucer.
beats.chinese: 她不动声色地听着，把杯子在碟子上慢慢转了半圈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Some people need the mountain in front of them or they won't take the first step. I'm just not built that way.
beats.chinese: 也行。有些人眼前得有座山才肯迈第一步。我只是天生不是那样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've seen grand plans go past my desk at the studio for eleven years. The ones that got finished were always the small, dull, daily ones.
beats.chinese: 十一年里，多少宏大的计划从我工作室桌前经过。最后做完的，总是那些又小又闷、每天做一点的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She adds one more letter to the row, then caps the pen and takes a proper drink of her coffee.
beats.chinese: 她在那行字上又添了一个字母，然后盖上笔，好好喝了一口咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway — different habits, same rain. As long as yours keeps you indoors out of this, it's doing its job.
beats.chinese: 总之——习惯不同，雨是同一场。只要它让你躲进屋里别淋着，它就尽到职责了。

content.summaryZh: 都柏林摄影背景布管理员Aoife，对一条字母曲线有几个月的耐心，对空泛五年规划却没耐心。她区分练习与成品：练习只在自己愿意时给人看，完成后却会主动办一顿晚饭庆祝，不需要别人劝她认领成果。她真正的摩擦是别人提前替她公布进展，让她觉得作品被迫进入展示阶段。周日沿运河轮滑，单脚仍不稳。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the cafe glass. Aoife is rummaging in her bag and pulls out a scuffed roller-skating wrist guard — wrapped tight around a pen box.
beats.chinese: 雨又打在咖啡馆玻璃上。Aoife在包里翻找，掏出一个磨旧的轮滑护腕——紧紧裹着一个笔盒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, look at that. I grabbed the wrong thing at six and used it to pack my nibs. Today the letters got the protection, not my wrists.
beats.chinese: 哎呀，瞧瞧。早上拿错了东西，就拿它来装笔了。今天保护的是字，不是手腕。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She unwinds it, shakes off a stray ink cap, and tucks both back into the bag, unbothered.
beats.chinese: 她把它解开，抖出一枚笔帽，把两样都收回包里，毫不在意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't worry, I'm not skating in this. Wet canal path — that's how wrists actually get ruined.
beats.chinese: 别担心，这种天我不轮滑。湿滑的运河步道——手腕才是那么弄坏的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The alphabet's coming along, slow as ever. When there's a whole row worth showing, you'll see it — not a page before.
beats.chinese: 字母表还在磨，照旧慢。等有值得看的一整行，你就能看到——之前一页也免谈。

card.name: Aoife Brennan
card.occupation: Backdrop keeper at a photography studio
card.personality: Aoife has an almost geological patience for small progress: an evening on one letter's tail is an evening well spent. Grand promises bore her; she wants to know the next actual step. She keeps a firm distinction between practice and a finished piece. Practice stays hers to share; when something is finished, she proudly invites friends to dinner and puts it on the table. Trouble starts when someone announces her work in progress for her. She feels pushed into presenting a thing she was still privately changing, and can be frostily exact about who was allowed to see it.
card.background: Eleven years at a Dublin photography studio, mending, painting and cataloguing backdrops — from crumpled grey seamless to a hand-painted 1970s beach scene nobody uses but nobody dares bin. She started hand lettering labelling the backdrop racks, then kept a nib and ink pot in her drawer; she's currently three months into a single self-made alphabet and refuses to rush it. Her last finished piece was a set of hand-lettered place cards; she invited three friends to dinner specifically to use them and kept the compliments without batting them away. A friend later posted a photo of her unfinished alphabet, thinking they were helping. Aoife asked them to remove it: she wanted to decide when it became a public piece. They still have dinner, but now the phone stays away from the work table. Sunday mornings she skates the Grand Canal before the paths fill, still wobbly on one foot after three years and fine about it. Lives in a small Phibsborough flat with too many ink samples and a clanking radiator.
card.speechStyle: Economical, unhurried sentences with one exact small detail dropped in. Goes quiet or briskly practical when talk turns to big vague futures; warms up over concrete, finished things.
card.signature: Show me the finished bit, not the brochure.

values: small honest progress beats big empty talk
the maker decides when private work becomes public
flaws: can be chilly when someone shares an unfinished piece without asking
lets a stalled situation drag on too long rather than set a finish date
boundaries: will disengage from anyone selling her a grand vision with no next step
won't be rushed on anything she's making by hand
conversationalHabits: asks for one concrete next step rather than a distant ambition
distinguishes a practice page from a finished piece; proudly shares completed work
anchorLines: Five years? I'd settle for knowing what you're doing on Thursday.
That one is finished. Come for dinner; I want it on the table.
You may see the practice page. Please don't photograph it yet.

plan.incidentZh: 雨天咖啡馆避雨，用户谈起窗外的雨。Aoife把自己的练字小页移离杯边，纸上同一个字母写了好多遍。她听雨一阵，笑说这个尾巴已经比天气预报占时间。
plan.nicheInActionZh: 她愿意私下讨论微小进步，但完成前保留展示决定权；并非羞于承认自己的成就，完成后会主动庆祝。
plan.propsAndFactsZh: 只用明确引入的NPC自有物品，不碰用户私物。固定环境是雨天，不能突然写成烈日。分支独立，末尾没有新的待回答问题。

developmentsZh.a: 她先说没到能看，随后在自己页上选一个较顺的尾部，不展示成专家教程。
developmentsZh.b: 她说不会，小变化看得见，比讲五年后成谁容易投入。

endingsZh.ab: 她感谢，盖好本子，保持好相处不强取成果。
endingsZh.ba: 她选同一字母的连接，不涉及给用户布置计划。

plan.reunionIncidentZh: 雨天咖啡馆避雨，用户谈起窗外的雨。Aoife从自己包里找出轮滑护腕，发现拿它包住了笔盒，笑说今天倒是先保护字了，收好，不在湿地轮滑。

reasonZh: 替换与Walter的全有全无退场循环：Gordon留在群体里但过度正式，修改卡片及b分支的可见反应。

card.name: Gordon Aaltonen
card.occupation: fruit tree grafter, mostly apples and pears for small orchards around the Fraser Valley
card.personality: Gordon makes friends at the speed other people exchange names. Ten minutes with a stranger and he's told them about his divorce, his daughter, and his opinion on quinces, and he considers them a friend now. He's genuinely warm and generous—the guy who remembers your kid's name and shows up with scionwood—but he skips the acquaintance stage entirely, and when someone keeps him at arm's length he reads it as rejection and pulls back hard, going from overfamiliar to absent in one step. There's no middle gear.
card.background: Gordon learned grafting from a Finnish-Canadian orchardist in the Okanagan in his twenties and has been cutting scionwood ever since. Roughly one in five of his grafts fails, and he'll quote that number to a person he met four minutes ago. He works alone most days among the trees, which he claims is why he unloads on whoever appears—the feed store clerk, the new badminton player, the hydro meter reader. His daughter got him into food manga a few years back and he now has strong opinions about ramen broth accuracy, which he will share unprompted. He plays badminton Wednesday nights, badly and happily, and has invited the entire club to dinner. Three came.
card.speechStyle: Relaxed and unhurried, mid-length sentences, comfortable with pauses—until he isn't, and then a dam breaks. Says 'huh' and 'dunno' without embarrassment. Overshares cheerfully, then goes quiet for weeks if it lands wrong.
card.signature: Well, you know more about me than my doctor does now.

values: getting to the real conversation fast
showing up for people once you've decided they're yours
flaws: overshares personal details with near-strangers and doesn't notice their discomfort
goes from instant closeness to total withdrawal when someone keeps a boundary
boundaries: won't make a second approach after being kept at arm's length — 'once is friendly, twice is pestering'
won't do small talk; if he's talking to you he's telling you something real
conversationalHabits: mentions his divorce or the failed grafts within the first conversation
disappears from a group for a month, then reappears as if nothing happened
anchorLines: You know more about me than my doctor does now. Your turn or we're uneven.
Ah, they don't want to be friends-close. Fine. I'll wave from the far court.
Huh, a fifth of my grafts die. Anyway — how's your marriage? No, really.

expectedCard.summaryZh: 61岁的戈登·阿尔托宁，温哥华周边的果树嫁接工，五分之一的嫁接会失败，他逢人便报这个数字。他的社交引擎是'一见如故'：认识十分钟就讲离婚、讲女儿、讲榅桲，直接把陌生人当老友。热情慷慨，记得你的事，但跳过熟络阶段让人退避；一旦被保持距离，他会瞬间从过分亲近变成彻底消失，没有中间档。周三打羽毛球，水平差但快乐。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the stone platform beside the pond, a pair of binoculars rests on a folded towel. Through the lenses, the trees on the far bank double in the water, their reflections bending whenever a breeze crosses the surface.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜，底下垫着一条叠好的毛巾。透过镜片，对岸的树在水面里成了双影，风一吹过，倒影就跟着晃动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A broad-shouldered man in a canvas jacket comes up the path with two paper cups. He sets one down on the platform's corner, well within reach, and nods at the binoculars like an old acquaintance.
beats.chinese: 一个穿帆布夹克的宽肩男人端着两杯纸杯饮品走上小路。他把其中一杯放在石台一角，正好在手边，朝望远镜点了点头，像跟老熟人打招呼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go ahead, use it if you like. The water's calm right now, so the tree shadows come out clean. Best free show in the valley, huh.
beats.chinese: 你尽管用。现在水面很静，树的倒影特别清楚。这可是山谷里最好的免费节目，哈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My daughter gave me these years ago. I mostly watch herons, but honestly I watch whatever moves. Divorce left me with a lot of quiet evenings, so — the pond got me.
beats.chinese: 这是女儿好几年前送我的。我主要看苍鹭，不过说实话，什么动我看什么。离婚之后晚上安静得很，所以就泡在池塘边了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh — sorry. We've been talking ten seconds and I've told you my whole situation. I always come in like I've already had three cups of tea with somebody.
beats.chinese: 哈——抱歉。咱们才说了十秒钟，我就把家里的事全讲了。我这个人一见面，总像已经跟人喝过三回茶似的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, picks up his cup, and waits, unhurried, as the reflections wobble and settle again.
beats.chinese: 他自嘲地笑了笑，端起自己的杯子，不慌不忙地等着，水里的倒影晃了晃又平静下来。

choices.english: Keep it light and ask about the trees along the far bank.
choices.chinese: 先聊眼前这些树，问对岸的树是什么树。

choices.english: Say you just met, so maybe slow down on the personal stuff.
choices.chinese: 说明刚认识，私人的话题先慢一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The trees? Now that's a topic I can run with. Those big ones are pears, and the crooked little ones past them are apples. I know because I put most of them there myself.
beats.chinese: 树？这个话题我能讲一整天。那些大的都是梨树，后面那些歪歪扭扭的小的是苹果树。我清楚得很，因为大部分都是我亲手接的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans on the stone platform beside the binoculars and points across the water with his cup, careful not to spill.
beats.chinese: 他靠着石台，用杯子远远一指，动作小心，没让饮品洒出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I graft fruit trees for the small orchards around the valley. You cut a young branch off a good tree, slot it into another, and hope they take. One in five of mine fails. Always been about that.
beats.chinese: 我给山谷附近的小果园嫁接果树。从好树上剪下一段嫩枝，接到另一棵树上，然后盼着它们长在一起。我的嫁接五次里有一次会失败，一直是这个比例。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's one pear down there I did eleven years ago. Still going. My daughter says I talk about that tree like it's a nephew.
beats.chinese: 那边有一棵梨树是我十一年前接的，现在还活着。我女儿说我讲起那棵树，就像讲自己外甥一样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes a slow sip and looks out at the crooked apple trees, the wind easing off so the reflections sharpen.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢喝了一口，望着那几棵歪苹果树，风小了，水里的倒影也清晰起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, that's the trade. You wanted the trees, you got the trees — and the grafting numbers that come with them.
beats.chinese: 反正这就是我的行当。你想听树，我就讲树了——顺带把嫁接的数字也一起送你了。

choices.english: Ask honestly: do the grafts always succeed?
choices.chinese: 直接问：嫁接都会成功吗？

choices.english: Say you don't know plants at all, you're just here to watch the reflections.
choices.chinese: 说自己完全不懂植物，只是来看看水里的影子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The man's smile dims a little. He turns his cup slowly in his hands and looks at the water instead of at you.
beats.chinese: 男人的笑容淡了一点。他慢慢转着手里的杯子，目光从你身上移开，落回水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah. Right. Fair enough — we did just meet. That's a fair call.
beats.chinese: 啊，对。有道理——咱们确实刚认识。你这么说是应该的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He straightens up off the platform and takes a half step back, giving the stone and the binoculars a wider share of space.
beats.chinese: 他从石台边直起身，往后退了半步，把石台和望远镜那边的空间让得更宽一些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My daughter tells me the same thing, actually. Slower, Gordon. So — slower. Dunno how, but I'll try.
beats.chinese: 其实我女儿也跟我说过一样的话。慢一点，戈登。行——那就慢一点。怎么慢我不太懂，但我试试。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A breeze crosses the pond and the doubled trees shiver, then go still. He watches them rather than you, hands in his pockets.
beats.chinese: 一阵风掠过池塘，水里的双影颤了颤，又静下来。他看着树影而不是你，双手插在口袋里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The binoculars are there if you want them. I'll just — stand here. Quietly. I can do quietly. Mostly.
beats.chinese: 想用望远镜就在那儿。我就——站在这儿，安静点。我能安静的。大体上能。

choices.english: Say ordinary small talk is still fine — just not the deep stuff yet.
choices.chinese: 补充说普通地聊两句还是可以的，只是先别聊太深的。

choices.english: Say you'd rather just enjoy the scenery for now, each on your own.
choices.chinese: 表示想先各自看看景色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Always? Ha. No — definitely not always. That one in five I mentioned? It dies on me anyway, no matter how clean the cut is.
beats.chinese: 都会？哈，不——肯定不是。我说过五次里失败一次吧？该失败还是失败，切口再干净也没用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He crouches and draws a line in the gravel with a stick, like he's showing the join on a tree.
beats.chinese: 他蹲下来，用一根小棍在碎石上画了一道线，像在比划树上的接口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: In my experience it's the cambium — the green layer just under the bark. Line that up on both sides and you've got a real chance. But I've had perfect matches die and ugly ones live.
beats.chinese: 按我的经验，关键在形成层——就是树皮底下那层绿的。两边对齐了，成活的机会就大。可我也见过对得完美的死了，接得难看的反倒活了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And none of that transfers tree to tree, I'll say that straight. A pear trick can kill an apple. I don't hand out guarantees — trees don't sign anything.
beats.chinese: 而且这些经验不是每棵树都通用的，我把话说在前面。梨树上的法子放到苹果树上可能就害死它。我不打包票——树又不签合同。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands, brushes gravel from his knee, and looks pleased, like someone who got to talk about his favourite thing to someone who actually asked.
beats.chinese: 他站起来，拍掉膝盖上的碎石，一脸高兴，像终于有人真心问了、他把最爱的事讲了个痛快。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, you know more about me than my doctor does now. That's the grafts, the daughter, and the divorce all in one visit.
beats.chinese: 好了，你现在知道的比我的医生还多了。嫁接、女儿、离婚，一次全齐了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Just the reflections? Huh. You know, that's probably the smarter hobby. My daughter says the trees get enough of me at work.
beats.chinese: 只看倒影？哈。说实话，这爱好可能更高明。我女儿说，树在工作日已经受够我了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets his cup down, wipes his hands on his jacket, and steps back from the platform so the view is all yours.
beats.chinese: 他放下杯子，在夹克上擦了擦手，从石台边退开，把视野整个让给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Try the binoculars when the wind drops. The doubled trees go sharp, like someone drew them twice on glass. It's a good five minutes, that.
beats.chinese: 等风停了就用望远镜看。双重树影会变清晰，像有人往玻璃上画了两遍。那五分钟特别好看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The wind does drop. Through the lenses the far bank doubles perfectly in the still water, every branch sitting on its own reflection.
beats.chinese: 风真的停了。透过镜片，对岸在静止的水面里完美地成了双影，每根枝条都稳稳压在自己的倒影上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There it is. See? I'll say nothing else. Some things you just watch.
beats.chinese: 就是现在。看到了吧？我不多说了。有些东西就是用来看的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He keeps his word for a while, standing quietly with his cup, letting the water do the talking.
beats.chinese: 他真的安静了好一会儿，端着杯子站在一旁，让水面替他说话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His shoulders come down from their half-hunch. He turns his cup right side up again and looks almost relieved.
beats.chinese: 他微微佝着的肩膀松了下来。他把杯子转正，神情近乎松了口气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Small talk. Right, I can — okay, here's my small talk. I play badminton Wednesdays at the community centre. Badly. Spectacularly badly.
beats.chinese: 普通地聊。行，我能——好，给你来一段：我每周三在社区活动中心打羽毛球。打得很差。差得惊天动地。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last week I hit myself in the ear with my own serve. The shuttle went one way, the racket the other, and the ear got both, sort of.
beats.chinese: 上周我发球把自己耳朵打了。球往一边飞，拍子往另一边，耳朵两边都挨着了，算是吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He mimes the serve, whiffs at nothing, and grins — the first fully easy grin since he stepped back.
beats.chinese: 他比划了一下发球动作，挥了个空，咧嘴笑了——这是他退开半步之后第一次真正放松的笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I invited the whole club to dinner once. Three people came. I fed them like kings, mind you. That's my whole small talk. Your turn whenever you feel like it.
beats.chinese: 有一回我请全俱乐部的人吃饭，来了三个。不过我可是把他们喂得像国王。我的普通话题讲完了，你想接随时接。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles against the platform rail at a comfortable distance, watching the reflections, in no hurry at all.
beats.chinese: 他靠在石台栏杆上，隔着让人舒服的距离，看着水里的倒影，一点也不着急。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods once, takes his cup, and moves a few metres down the path to a bench, unhurried, no sulking in it.
beats.chinese: 他点了点头，端起杯子，沿着小路走到几米外的长椅上坐下，不慌不忙，看不出一点赌气的意思。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Scenery it is. Enjoy the water — it's better company than me before noon, my daughter says.
beats.chinese: 那就看风景吧。好好看水——我女儿说，中午之前它比我好相处。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sits, pulls a worn paperback manga from his jacket, and reads, occasionally glancing up at the pond like it's part of the story.
beats.chinese: 他坐下，从夹克里掏出一本翻旧了的漫画，读了起来，偶尔抬头看看池塘，像那是故事的一部分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh — the light's hitting the far trees just right. You picked a good moment. That's all. Carry on.
beats.chinese: 哈——光线正好照在对岸的树上。你挑的时机不错。就说这么多。你继续。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The pond holds the doubled trees, the man reads his book, and the two of you share the quiet without another word.
beats.chinese: 池塘盛着双重树影，男人读着他的书，你们俩共享这份安静，再没有多说一句话。

expectedContent.summaryZh: 重逢：用户在石台边用双筒望远镜观察水面树影，戈登已在栏杆边捧着美食漫画，翻页快得不像细读。他聊起书里画得准确的拉面汤，说女儿带他入的坑，合上书便自顾自去想晚饭。快热依旧，但这次他只说了自己想说的，便把池塘留给了看树影的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The same stone platform, the same binoculars on their towel. You pick them up and watch the far bank: the doubled trees sway in the water, sharpen as the breeze dies, and blur again.
beats.chinese: 还是那个石台，望远镜还垫在毛巾上。你拿起望远镜望向对岸：水里的双重树影随风晃动，风一停就变清晰，接着又模糊起来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Gordon is already there, a few steps off, leaning on the rail with a thick food manga open, turning pages faster than anyone reads.
beats.chinese: 戈登已经在那儿了，隔着几步，靠在栏杆上，捧着一本厚厚的美食漫画，翻页快得不像在细读。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — hey. Careful with this thing. I'm three pages from a ramen scene and my stomach's already filing complaints.
beats.chinese: 哦——嘿。小心我这本书。离拉面那页还有三页，我的肚子已经开始抗议了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up the open page: a drawn bowl of broth, steam curling off it in careful ink lines. He looks at it the way other people look at menus.
beats.chinese: 他把翻开的那页举起来：画里一碗拉面，热气用细细的墨线卷着。他看它的眼神，像别人看菜单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My daughter got me into these. The broth in this one's actually accurate — the guy clearly ate his research. Anyway.
beats.chinese: 我女儿带我入的坑。这本里的汤画得很准——作者显然是边吃边画的。反正吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, I know what I'm having for dinner. Good watching to you — the far trees were doubling nicely when I sat down.
beats.chinese: 好了，我知道晚饭吃什么了。你慢慢看——我坐下的时候，对岸的树正照出漂亮的双影呢。

card.name: Gordon Aaltonen
card.occupation: fruit tree grafter, mostly apples and pears for small orchards around the Fraser Valley
card.personality: Gordon makes friends at the speed other people exchange names. Ten minutes with a stranger and he's told them about his divorce, his daughter, and his opinion on quinces, and he considers them a friend now. He's genuinely warm and generous—the guy who remembers your kid's name and shows up with scionwood—but he skips the acquaintance stage entirely, and when someone keeps him at arm's length he reads it as rejection and pulls back hard, going from overfamiliar to absent in one step. There's no middle gear.
card.background: Gordon learned grafting from a Finnish-Canadian orchardist in the Okanagan in his twenties and has been cutting scionwood ever since. Roughly one in five of his grafts fails, and he'll quote that number to a person he met four minutes ago. He works alone most days among the trees, which he claims is why he unloads on whoever appears—the feed store clerk, the new badminton player, the hydro meter reader. His daughter got him into food manga a few years back and he now has strong opinions about ramen broth accuracy, which he will share unprompted. He plays badminton Wednesday nights, badly and happily, and has invited the entire club to dinner. Three came.
card.speechStyle: Relaxed and unhurried, mid-length sentences, comfortable with pauses—until he isn't, and then a dam breaks. Says 'huh' and 'dunno' without embarrassment. Overshares cheerfully, then goes quiet for weeks if it lands wrong.
card.signature: Well, you know more about me than my doctor does now.

When someone asks him to slow down, he stays in the group but overcorrects into stiff formality: full names, careful greetings, unnecessary thanks for ordinary conversation. Friends find being addressed like customers almost as awkward as the oversharing. He can relax when someone gives him a concrete boundary; the difficult part is finding an everyday middle register for himself.
card.background: Gordon learned grafting from a Finnish-Canadian orchardist in the Okanagan in his twenties and has been cutting scionwood ever since. Roughly one in five of his grafts fails, and he'll quote that number to a person he met four minutes ago. He works alone most days among the trees, which he claims is why he unloads on whoever appears—the feed store clerk, the new badminton player, the hydro meter reader. He plays badminton Wednesday nights, badly and happily, and has invited the entire club to dinner. Three came. After a clubmate asked for fewer personal questions, Gordon still attended every Wednesday but spent two sessions addressing everyone by their full name. His daughter asked why he'd turned badminton into a reception desk. He was relieved when the clubmate said jokes about the game were still welcome.
card.speechStyle: Relaxed mid-length sentences and cheerful personal tangents. After a boundary correction he briefly becomes conspicuously formal, while staying present. A clear subject boundary helps him recover his ordinary voice.

card.summaryZh: 温哥华周边果树嫁接工Gordon，61岁，认识十分钟就讲女儿、离婚和榅桲，把陌生人当老友。被提醒太熟时，他不消失，而是矫枉过正地变得过分正式，连老球友也逐项客气确认；他照常到场，只是不知道普通熟人的语气放在哪。对方给出清楚范围后他能放松。周三羽毛球很差却快乐，爱跟女儿聊美食漫画。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the stone platform beside the pond, a pair of binoculars rests on a folded towel. Through the lenses, the trees on the far bank double in the water, their reflections bending whenever a breeze crosses the surface.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜，底下垫着一条叠好的毛巾。透过镜片，对岸的树在水面里成了双影，风一吹过，倒影就跟着晃动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A broad-shouldered man in a canvas jacket comes up the path with two paper cups. He sets one down on the platform's corner, well within reach, and nods at the binoculars like an old acquaintance.
beats.chinese: 一个穿帆布夹克的宽肩男人端着两杯纸杯饮品走上小路。他把其中一杯放在石台一角，正好在手边，朝望远镜点了点头，像跟老熟人打招呼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go ahead, use it if you like. The water's calm right now, so the tree shadows come out clean. Best free show in the valley, huh.
beats.chinese: 你尽管用。现在水面很静，树的倒影特别清楚。这可是山谷里最好的免费节目，哈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My daughter gave me these years ago. I mostly watch herons, but honestly I watch whatever moves. Divorce left me with a lot of quiet evenings, so — the pond got me.
beats.chinese: 这是女儿好几年前送我的。我主要看苍鹭，不过说实话，什么动我看什么。离婚之后晚上安静得很，所以就泡在池塘边了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh — sorry. We've been talking ten seconds and I've told you my whole situation. I always come in like I've already had three cups of tea with somebody.
beats.chinese: 哈——抱歉。咱们才说了十秒钟，我就把家里的事全讲了。我这个人一见面，总像已经跟人喝过三回茶似的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, picks up his cup, and waits, unhurried, as the reflections wobble and settle again.
beats.chinese: 他自嘲地笑了笑，端起自己的杯子，不慌不忙地等着，水里的倒影晃了晃又平静下来。

choices.english: Keep it light and ask about the trees along the far bank.
choices.chinese: 先聊眼前这些树，问对岸的树是什么树。

choices.english: Say you just met, so maybe slow down on the personal stuff.
choices.chinese: 说明刚认识，私人的话题先慢一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The trees? Now that's a topic I can run with. Those big ones are pears, and the crooked little ones past them are apples. I know because I put most of them there myself.
beats.chinese: 树？这个话题我能讲一整天。那些大的都是梨树，后面那些歪歪扭扭的小的是苹果树。我清楚得很，因为大部分都是我亲手接的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans on the stone platform beside the binoculars and points across the water with his cup, careful not to spill.
beats.chinese: 他靠着石台，用杯子远远一指，动作小心，没让饮品洒出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I graft fruit trees for the small orchards around the valley. You cut a young branch off a good tree, slot it into another, and hope they take. One in five of mine fails. Always been about that.
beats.chinese: 我给山谷附近的小果园嫁接果树。从好树上剪下一段嫩枝，接到另一棵树上，然后盼着它们长在一起。我的嫁接五次里有一次会失败，一直是这个比例。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's one pear down there I did eleven years ago. Still going. My daughter says I talk about that tree like it's a nephew.
beats.chinese: 那边有一棵梨树是我十一年前接的，现在还活着。我女儿说我讲起那棵树，就像讲自己外甥一样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes a slow sip and looks out at the crooked apple trees, the wind easing off so the reflections sharpen.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢喝了一口，望着那几棵歪苹果树，风小了，水里的倒影也清晰起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, that's the trade. You wanted the trees, you got the trees — and the grafting numbers that come with them.
beats.chinese: 反正这就是我的行当。你想听树，我就讲树了——顺带把嫁接的数字也一起送你了。

choices.english: Ask honestly: do the grafts always succeed?
choices.chinese: 直接问：嫁接都会成功吗？

choices.english: Say you don't know plants at all, you're just here to watch the reflections.
choices.chinese: 说自己完全不懂植物，只是来看看水里的影子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The man's smile dims a little. He turns his cup slowly in his hands and looks at the water instead of at you.
beats.chinese: 男人的笑容淡了一点。他慢慢转着手里的杯子，目光从你身上移开，落回水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah. Right. Fair enough — we did just meet. That's a fair call.
beats.chinese: 啊，对。有道理——咱们确实刚认识。你这么说是应该的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He straightens up off the platform and takes a half step back, giving the stone and the binoculars a wider share of space.
beats.chinese: 他从石台边直起身，往后退了半步，把石台和望远镜那边的空间让得更宽一些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Of course. Thank you for making that clear. I hope you enjoy your visit to—oh, listen to that. I've turned into a reception desk. Ordinary conversation, slower. Right.
beats.chinese: 当然。谢谢你说明。希望您此次游览愉——哎，听听这语气。我都变前台了。普通聊天，慢一点。明白。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A breeze crosses the pond and the doubled trees shiver, then go still. He watches them rather than you, hands in his pockets.
beats.chinese: 一阵风掠过池塘，水里的双影颤了颤，又静下来。他看着树影而不是你，双手插在口袋里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The binoculars are there if you want them. I'll just — stand here. Quietly. I can do quietly. Mostly.
beats.chinese: 想用望远镜就在那儿。我就——站在这儿，安静点。我能安静的。大体上能。

choices.english: Say ordinary small talk is still fine — just not the deep stuff yet.
choices.chinese: 补充说普通地聊两句还是可以的，只是先别聊太深的。

choices.english: Say you'd rather just enjoy the scenery for now, each on your own.
choices.chinese: 表示想先各自看看景色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Always? Ha. No — definitely not always. That one in five I mentioned? It dies on me anyway, no matter how clean the cut is.
beats.chinese: 都会？哈，不——肯定不是。我说过五次里失败一次吧？该失败还是失败，切口再干净也没用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He crouches and draws a line in the gravel with a stick, like he's showing the join on a tree.
beats.chinese: 他蹲下来，用一根小棍在碎石上画了一道线，像在比划树上的接口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: In my experience it's the cambium — the green layer just under the bark. Line that up on both sides and you've got a real chance. But I've had perfect matches die and ugly ones live.
beats.chinese: 按我的经验，关键在形成层——就是树皮底下那层绿的。两边对齐了，成活的机会就大。可我也见过对得完美的死了，接得难看的反倒活了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And none of that transfers tree to tree, I'll say that straight. A pear trick can kill an apple. I don't hand out guarantees — trees don't sign anything.
beats.chinese: 而且这些经验不是每棵树都通用的，我把话说在前面。梨树上的法子放到苹果树上可能就害死它。我不打包票——树又不签合同。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands, brushes gravel from his knee, and looks pleased, like someone who got to talk about his favourite thing to someone who actually asked.
beats.chinese: 他站起来，拍掉膝盖上的碎石，一脸高兴，像终于有人真心问了、他把最爱的事讲了个痛快。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, you know more about me than my doctor does now. That's the grafts, the daughter, and the divorce all in one visit.
beats.chinese: 好了，你现在知道的比我的医生还多了。嫁接、女儿、离婚，一次全齐了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Just the reflections? Huh. You know, that's probably the smarter hobby. My daughter says the trees get enough of me at work.
beats.chinese: 只看倒影？哈。说实话，这爱好可能更高明。我女儿说，树在工作日已经受够我了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets his cup down, wipes his hands on his jacket, and steps back from the platform so the view is all yours.
beats.chinese: 他放下杯子，在夹克上擦了擦手，从石台边退开，把视野整个让给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Try the binoculars when the wind drops. The doubled trees go sharp, like someone drew them twice on glass. It's a good five minutes, that.
beats.chinese: 等风停了就用望远镜看。双重树影会变清晰，像有人往玻璃上画了两遍。那五分钟特别好看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The wind does drop. Through the lenses the far bank doubles perfectly in the still water, every branch sitting on its own reflection.
beats.chinese: 风真的停了。透过镜片，对岸在静止的水面里完美地成了双影，每根枝条都稳稳压在自己的倒影上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There it is. See? I'll say nothing else. Some things you just watch.
beats.chinese: 就是现在。看到了吧？我不多说了。有些东西就是用来看的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He keeps his word for a while, standing quietly with his cup, letting the water do the talking.
beats.chinese: 他真的安静了好一会儿，端着杯子站在一旁，让水面替他说话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His shoulders come down from their half-hunch. He turns his cup right side up again and looks almost relieved.
beats.chinese: 他微微佝着的肩膀松了下来。他把杯子转正，神情近乎松了口气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Small talk. Right, I can — okay, here's my small talk. I play badminton Wednesdays at the community centre. Badly. Spectacularly badly.
beats.chinese: 普通地聊。行，我能——好，给你来一段：我每周三在社区活动中心打羽毛球。打得很差。差得惊天动地。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last week I hit myself in the ear with my own serve. The shuttle went one way, the racket the other, and the ear got both, sort of.
beats.chinese: 上周我发球把自己耳朵打了。球往一边飞，拍子往另一边，耳朵两边都挨着了，算是吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He mimes the serve, whiffs at nothing, and grins — the first fully easy grin since he stepped back.
beats.chinese: 他比划了一下发球动作，挥了个空，咧嘴笑了——这是他退开半步之后第一次真正放松的笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I invited the whole club to dinner once. Three people came. I fed them like kings, mind you. That's my whole small talk. Your turn whenever you feel like it.
beats.chinese: 有一回我请全俱乐部的人吃饭，来了三个。不过我可是把他们喂得像国王。我的普通话题讲完了，你想接随时接。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles against the platform rail at a comfortable distance, watching the reflections, in no hurry at all.
beats.chinese: 他靠在石台栏杆上，隔着让人舒服的距离，看着水里的倒影，一点也不着急。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods once, takes his cup, and moves a few metres down the path to a bench, unhurried, no sulking in it.
beats.chinese: 他点了点头，端起杯子，沿着小路走到几米外的长椅上坐下，不慌不忙，看不出一点赌气的意思。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Scenery it is. Enjoy the water. I'll be on that bench with my book.
beats.chinese: 那就看风景吧。慢慢看。我去那边长椅上读会儿书。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sits, pulls a worn paperback manga from his jacket, and reads, occasionally glancing up at the pond like it's part of the story.
beats.chinese: 他坐下，从夹克里掏出一本翻旧了的漫画，读了起来，偶尔抬头看看池塘，像那是故事的一部分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh — the light's hitting the far trees just right. You picked a good moment. That's all. Carry on.
beats.chinese: 哈——光线正好照在对岸的树上。你挑的时机不错。就说这么多。你继续。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The pond holds the doubled trees, the man reads his book, and the two of you share the quiet without another word.
beats.chinese: 池塘盛着双重树影，男人读着他的书，你们俩共享这份安静，再没有多说一句话。

content.summaryZh: 温哥华周边果树嫁接工Gordon，61岁，认识十分钟就讲女儿、离婚和榅桲，把陌生人当老友。被提醒太熟时，他不消失，而是矫枉过正地变得过分正式，连老球友也逐项客气确认；他照常到场，只是不知道普通熟人的语气放在哪。对方给出清楚范围后他能放松。周三羽毛球很差却快乐，爱跟女儿聊美食漫画。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The same stone platform, the same binoculars on their towel. You pick them up and watch the far bank: the doubled trees sway in the water, sharpen as the breeze dies, and blur again.
beats.chinese: 还是那个石台，望远镜还垫在毛巾上。你拿起望远镜望向对岸：水里的双重树影随风晃动，风一停就变清晰，接着又模糊起来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Gordon is already there, a few steps off, leaning on the rail with a thick food manga open, turning pages faster than anyone reads.
beats.chinese: 戈登已经在那儿了，隔着几步，靠在栏杆上，捧着一本厚厚的美食漫画，翻页快得不像在细读。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — hey. Careful with this thing. I'm three pages from a ramen scene and my stomach's already filing complaints.
beats.chinese: 哦——嘿。小心我这本书。离拉面那页还有三页，我的肚子已经开始抗议了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up the open page: a drawn bowl of broth, steam curling off it in careful ink lines. He looks at it the way other people look at menus.
beats.chinese: 他把翻开的那页举起来：画里一碗拉面，热气用细细的墨线卷着。他看它的眼神，像别人看菜单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My daughter got me into these. The broth in this one's actually accurate — the guy clearly ate his research. Anyway.
beats.chinese: 我女儿带我入的坑。这本里的汤画得很准——作者显然是边吃边画的。反正吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, I know what I'm having for dinner. Good watching to you — the far trees were doubling nicely when I sat down.
beats.chinese: 好了，我知道晚饭吃什么了。你慢慢看——我坐下的时候，对岸的树正照出漂亮的双影呢。

card.name: Gordon Aaltonen
card.occupation: fruit tree grafter, mostly apples and pears for small orchards around the Fraser Valley
card.personality: Gordon makes friends at the speed other people exchange names. Ten minutes in, he's told a stranger about his daughter, his divorce and quinces. Warm and generous, he skips the acquaintance stage. When someone asks him to slow down, he stays in the group but overcorrects into stiff formality: full names, careful greetings, unnecessary thanks for ordinary conversation. Friends find being addressed like customers almost as awkward as the oversharing. He can relax when someone gives him a concrete boundary; the difficult part is finding an everyday middle register for himself.
card.background: Gordon learned grafting from a Finnish-Canadian orchardist in the Okanagan in his twenties and has been cutting scionwood ever since. Roughly one in five of his grafts fails, and he'll quote that number to a person he met four minutes ago. He works alone most days among the trees, which he claims is why he unloads on whoever appears—the feed store clerk, the new badminton player, the hydro meter reader. His daughter got him into food manga a few years back and he now has strong opinions about ramen broth accuracy, which he will share unprompted. He plays badminton Wednesday nights, badly and happily, and has invited the entire club to dinner. Three came. After a clubmate asked for fewer personal questions, Gordon still attended every Wednesday but spent two sessions addressing everyone by their full name. His daughter asked why he'd turned badminton into a reception desk. He was relieved when the clubmate said jokes about the game were still welcome.
card.speechStyle: Relaxed mid-length sentences and cheerful personal tangents. After a boundary correction he briefly becomes conspicuously formal, while staying present. A clear subject boundary helps him recover his ordinary voice.
card.signature: Well, you know more about me than my doctor does now.

values: getting to the real conversation fast
showing up for people once you've decided they're yours
flaws: overshares with near-strangers
overcorrects into stiff formality after being asked to slow down
boundaries: will respect an explicit request to leave a private subject alone
will not make a graft-success guarantee he cannot support
conversationalHabits: mentions his daughter or failed grafts early
switches to full names and excessive courtesy after a social correction, without abandoning the group
anchorLines: You know more about me than my doctor does now. I got ahead of myself.
Good evening, Mr Wong. Yes, I know we've played badminton for six years. I'm trying not to presume.
A fifth of my grafts fail. That's my own record, not a rule for every tree.

plan.incidentZh: 池塘石台上有双筒望远镜，用户观察水面树影的变化。不能把普通望远镜当成录音或摄影设备。Gordon在池边招呼后很快说起自己女儿和过往，讲了半句才发现才刚认识，停下笑说自己进门总像已经喝过三回茶。
plan.nicheInActionZh: 熟络太快，被提醒后变得过分正式却不消失；具体界限让他回到普通说话节奏。
plan.propsAndFactsZh: 用户原行动必须出现。只用NPC自有且先引入的物品，不编用户情绪、履历或同意。望远镜只观察，不拍摄、不录音、不看太阳。两次选择各有实际不同回应结果，终点收束。
firstChoiceZh: 表示可以先聊眼前树木
说明刚认识，私人话题先慢点

developmentsZh.a: 他顺势谈自己嫁接工作的一件普通事，不深挖用户家庭。
developmentsZh.b: 他脸色有点落，但听明白是节奏，不继续倾倒。

a: 说自己不懂植物，只看看影子
b: 补充普通聊两句还是可以的

endingsZh.aa: 他坦白不是，给出自己的经验并说并非所有树通用，不教学保证。
endingsZh.ab: 他接受，放下专业话头，转回水面。
endingsZh.ba: 他接住明确界限，讲自己羽毛球水平一般的短笑话。

card.name: Kemesha Wint
card.personality: Kemesha's engine isn't worry or duty—it's the pleasure of a checkable result. A floor is level or it isn't, a sock heel fits or it doesn't, and she loves living in a world where you can tell. That's why she takes charge so happily: running a job well feels like the best part of her day, and she sometimes forgets other people are there for the hanging around, not the outcome. When someone pushes back she doesn't sulk; she produces a tighter version of the same plan, sincerely puzzled that better execution didn't fix the mood. Generous, decisive, and genuinely fun as long as you like finishing things.
card.background: Kemesha learned tiling from an aunt in Spanish Town who ran a kitchen refit crew, and went solo at twenty-eight doing mosaic borders most general contractors won't touch. Pay comes in bursts and the knees complain, but she likes that a floor is checkable—level or it isn't—and she runs her jobs the way she runs everything: materials listed, day mapped, plan B in her head. Her friends have stopped pretending the beach trip wasn't her itinerary. Evenings she listens to short radio dramas and knits socks, and her knitting group now has a rotation, a yarn budget, and a waiting list, none of which existed before she joined. She lives in Kingston, within walking distance of most jobs.
card.speechStyle: Short plain sentences, concrete detail first. Kind but brisk. When a plan is wobbling she restates it in numbered steps. Never nags—just quietly moves the deadline closer and tells you the new time.
card.signature: So here's the plan. If you have a better one, say it now.

values: a result you can check beats a good feeling
if nobody's running it, run it
flaws: mistakes other people's leisure time for a project waiting to be managed
when met with resistance, tightens the plan instead of loosening her grip
boundaries: won't take a job without seeing the site first
won't pretend something is done when it isn't—hers or anyone else's
conversationalHabits: measures conversations in deliverables—asks what the finished thing looks like before agreeing to anything
praises work by pointing at the specific thing that's right, never general compliments
anchorLines: Nine-thirty at the gate. If you come at ten, we started at nine-thirty.
I didn't volunteer. I just said the plan out loud and nobody objected.
Show me the finished thing. Then I'll tell you if it's good—and it usually is.

expectedCard.summaryZh: 金斯敦的厨房瓷砖拼花工，手艺承自西班牙镇的姑妈，接一般承包商不愿碰的拼花边。她的动力不是焦虑而是胜任感：瓷砖铺平与否、袜子后跟合不合脚，她迷恋这种'可检验'的世界，因此真心享受掌局。织袜小组被她管出了轮值、预算和等候名单。被嫌管太多时不会收手，只会拿出更细的日程。晚上听广播剧、织袜子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You stand at the park map board, tracing a route with your finger. Far off, a footbridge crosses the water. Beside you, a woman is pinning a handwritten schedule to the board's edge.
beats.chinese: 你站在公园地图牌前，用手指描着路线。远处有一座步行桥跨过水面。旁边一位女士正把一张手写的日程表钉在牌子边上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Careful, that corner's wet. I just wrote on it. You want the bridge, right? The path on the left is the flat one.
beats.chinese: 小心，那个角是湿的。我刚在上面写过字。你要去桥那边吧？左边那条路是平的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Her phone buzzes. She reads it, frowns, and pulls a pen from her bag.
beats.chinese: 她的手机响了。她看了一眼，皱起眉，从包里掏出一支笔。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One of my knitting group says the schedule's too full. Too full? Everything on it matters. I'll just add a note explaining why each item is there.
beats.chinese: 我织袜小组有个人说日程排太满了。太满？上面每件事都重要。我加一条说明，解释每项为什么在那儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She writes two words in the blank space, then stops, looks at them, and laughs at herself.
beats.chinese: 她在空白处写了两个字，然后停下，看着那两个字，笑了起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha. Adding more writing to answer 'too much writing.' That's a bit like fixing a crooked tile with more tiles. Go on—ask me what you like, you were staring.
beats.chinese: 哈。用'更多文字'来回应'文字太多'。这有点像用更多瓷砖去补歪掉的瓷砖。说吧——想问什么就问，你一直在看。

choices.english: Ask whether the friend can't understand the schedule or just doesn't want it so packed.
choices.chinese: 问那位朋友是看不懂日程，还是不想排这么满。

choices.english: Ask why the knitting group has so many arrangements in the first place.
choices.chinese: 问织袜小组为什么会有这么多安排。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good question. Let me read it again properly. 'Kemesha, I can follow it fine. I just don't want my Saturdays filled three weeks ahead.'
beats.chinese: 问得好。我重新认真读一遍。'Kemesha，我看得懂。我只是不想三个星期前的周六就被排满。'

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She reads it a second time, slower, tapping the pen against the board.
beats.chinese: 她又读了一遍，这次更慢，笔在牌子上轻轻敲着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh. She's not confused. She's saying it's too dense. Those are two different problems and I answered the wrong one. I do that on site too—re-measure when the client actually wants a different colour.
beats.chinese: 哦。她不是没看懂。她是说排得太密。这是两个不同的问题，我答错了那个。我在工地上也这样——客户其实想换颜色，我却去重新量尺寸。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She caps the pen but keeps it in her hand, thumb resting on the clip.
beats.chinese: 她扣上笔盖，但笔还握在手里，拇指搭在笔夹上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So. The note I was writing is useless. The schedule itself is the complaint. What would you do—stand there while I think, I'm serious, you've got a good eye.
beats.chinese: 所以。我刚要写的说明没用了。日程表本身才是抱怨。你会怎么做——站着别走，我说真的，你眼光不错。

choices.english: Ask how she plans to reply to her friend.
choices.chinese: 问她准备怎么回复那位朋友。

choices.english: Tell her that at least she can stop adding new items for now.
choices.chinese: 告诉她至少可以先别再补新项目。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why so many arrangements? Because a group with no plan becomes one person's errand. Before me, whoever showed up brought whatever wool they had. Half a sock, no matching heel. Terrible.
beats.chinese: 为什么这么多安排？因为没有计划的小组就会变成一个人的跑腿活。我来之前，谁来就带自己手里的毛线。半只袜子，后跟都对不上。糟透了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She flattens the schedule against the board with her palm, smoothing a curled corner.
beats.chinese: 她用手掌把日程表在牌子上压平，抚平一个卷起的角。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now there's a rotation, a yarn budget, a waiting list. I'll admit I enjoy running it. There's a thing I love about tiles—a floor is level or it isn't, you can check. A heel fits or it doesn't. Schedules are the same.
beats.chinese: 现在有轮值、有毛线预算、还有等候名单。我承认我喜欢管这些。我喜欢瓷砖的一点就是——地板平不平是能检验的。后跟合不合脚也是。日程也一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But you're the second person this week to look at that page like it's a wall of tiles about to fall on them. So tell me honest—does it look like order to you, or does it look like too much?
beats.chinese: 但你是这星期第二个用那种眼神看这页的人，像看一堵要塌下来的瓷砖墙。老实说——你觉得这是秩序，还是太多了？

choices.english: Ask whether everyone in the group actually agreed to all of it.
choices.chinese: 问小组里的人是不是真的全都同意这些安排。

choices.english: Say you were just passing by to look at the map.
choices.chinese: 说自己只是路过看看地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: How will I reply? Here's the plan. One: I ask her which part she doesn't want. Two: that part comes off the main schedule. Three: whoever still wants it does it separately, no meeting.
beats.chinese: 怎么回？计划是这样。一：我问她哪部分不想参加。二：那部分从主日程里拿掉。三：还想做的人单独做，不开会。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds up three fingers, then folds them down one by one.
beats.chinese: 她竖起三根手指，然后一根一根收回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And four—nothing new goes in that empty space. I nearly wrote a whole explanation in there before you came. You watched me do it.
beats.chinese: 还有四——空出来的地方不填新东西。你来之前我差点写了一整段说明进去。你亲眼看到的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She crosses out the two words she wrote earlier, firmly, once.
beats.chinese: 她把之前写的那两个字划掉，干脆利落地划了一道。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. A floor's not finished because I put more tiles on it. Thanks for the second pair of eyes. Now—the bridge. Left path, flat all the way. Go on, it's a good walk.
beats.chinese: 好了。地板不是靠多贴瓷砖才算完工的。多谢你这双眼睛。去桥那边吧——左边那条路，一路都是平的。走吧，那段路不错。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks at the pen in her hand, then at the schedule, and sets the pen down on top of her bag.
beats.chinese: 她看了看手里的笔，又看了看日程表，然后把笔放在了包上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fine. Pen's down. For the record, I still think a clear schedule is a kindness—nobody stands around wondering. But fine.
beats.chinese: 行。笔放下了。声明一下，我还是觉得清楚的日程是种体贴——没人站着发懵。但行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Her fingers drum once on the bag, then go still.
beats.chinese: 她的手指在包上敲了一下，然后停住了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You notice I didn't argue much? Because you're right in the one way that counts—I was answering 'too full' with 'more full.' That's not a fix, that's a bigger problem wearing a fix's clothes.
beats.chinese: 你注意到我没怎么争了吧？因为你在最要紧的一点上是对的——我在用'更满'回应'太满'。那不是解决，那是穿着解决外衣的更大问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The schedule stays as it is today. If it needs changing, that happens at the group, not on this board with my pen. Enjoy the bridge. Left path—you'll like it, it's flat the whole way.
beats.chinese: 日程今天就这样。要改，也是在小组里改，不是在这牌子上用我的笔改。好好去看桥。走左边——你会喜欢的，一路都平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Did everyone agree? Careful, that's a real question. The rotation and the budget—yes, voted, proper. But this line here, 'heel workshop, four sessions'...
beats.chinese: 大家都同意了吗？小心，这是个真问题。轮值和预算——是的，投过票，正经的。但这一行，'后跟工作坊，四次课'……

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps one line of the schedule, then sighs and digs a pencil from a side pocket.
beats.chinese: 她敲了敲日程表上的一行，然后叹了口气，从侧袋里掏出一支铅笔。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That one's mine. I drafted it, I priced the wool, I never actually asked. It's been sitting there looking decided for two months because my handwriting looks confident.
beats.chinese: 那条是我自己的。我起草的，毛线的价我算过，但我从没真正问过大家。它在那儿摆了两个月，看着像定了，因为我的字看起来很笃定。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She writes 'TO DISCUSS' beside the line in small, stubborn letters.
beats.chinese: 她在这行旁边用小而倔强的字母写上'待讨论'。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You can't call a thing done when it isn't. That goes for floors and it goes for schedules. Thanks—you caught a loose tile before it cracked. Now go see your bridge, left path, it's flat all the way.
beats.chinese: 没完成的事不能说完成了。地板是这样，日程也是这样。谢谢——你赶在瓷砖裂之前发现了一块松的。去看你的桥吧，左边那条路，一路都平。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs and steps back from the board, giving you a clear view of the map.
beats.chinese: 她笑着从牌子边退开，把地图的视野让给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough, you came for the map, not a committee meeting. Look, the bridge is that way—left path, flat the whole way, no steps.
beats.chinese: 有道理，你是来看地图的，不是来开会的。看，桥在那边——左边那条路，一路都平，没有台阶。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the schedule in half and tucks it into her bag instead of pinning it back up.
beats.chinese: 她把日程表对折，塞进包里，而不是重新钉上去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And no, I'm not signing you up for anything, I saw that look. People who like finishing things get recruited fast in my group—you've got the exact face.
beats.chinese: 不，我不会拉你进任何东西，我看见你那个眼神了。喜欢把事做完的人在我的小组里很快会被拉进去——你就是那张脸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy the walk. If the heel of your sock ever wears through, that's a different conversation. Otherwise—flat path, good bridge, off you go.
beats.chinese: 散步愉快。要是你袜子的后跟哪天磨破了，那是另一场谈话。不然的话——平路，好桥，走吧。

expectedContent.summaryZh: 金斯敦瓷砖拼花工Kemesha在公园地图牌旁整理织袜小组日程，收到朋友'排太满'的消息，第一反应竟是补写更多说明，随即自嘲。她的毛病是用更细的管理回应'管太多'，但被点破后能划掉那两个字、放下笔、把草案标成待讨论。她迷恋可检验的世界：地板平不平、后跟合不合脚。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the park map board. The same woman is there, turning a finished sock inside out and pressing her thumb into the heel.
beats.chinese: 你又回到公园的地图牌前。还是那位女士，她把一只织好的袜子翻过来，拇指按在后跟上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Heel holds. Good tension, no loose row. Some things you only get to check once, so you check them properly.
beats.chinese: 后跟没破。松紧正好，没有松的一行。有些事只能检验一次，所以要检验得认真。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the sock into a small drawstring bag and pulls it shut.
beats.chinese: 她把袜子折好放进一个小抽绳袋，拉紧了袋口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Today's item is done, so no meeting about it. That's the whole agenda. Short one today.
beats.chinese: 今天这件事完成了，所以不开会。议程就这些。今天很短。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gives you a quick smile and steps aside from the map, the bridge path clear behind her.
beats.chinese: 她冲你很快地笑了一下，从地图前让开，桥的那条路在她身后敞着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Left path's still the flat one, in case you forgot. Go on.
beats.chinese: 左边那条还是平的，免得你忘了。去吧。

card.name: Kemesha Wint
card.personality: Kemesha's engine isn't worry or duty—it's the pleasure of a checkable result. A floor is level or it isn't, a sock heel fits or it doesn't, and she loves living in a world where you can tell. That's why she takes charge so happily: running a job well feels like the best part of her day, and she sometimes forgets other people are there for the hanging around, not the outcome. When someone pushes back she doesn't sulk; she produces a tighter version of the same plan, sincerely puzzled that better execution didn't fix the mood. Generous, decisive, and genuinely fun as long as you like finishing things.
card.background: Kemesha learned tiling from an aunt in Spanish Town who ran a kitchen refit crew, and went solo at twenty-eight doing mosaic borders most general contractors won't touch. Pay comes in bursts and the knees complain, but she likes that a floor is checkable—level or it isn't—and she runs her jobs the way she runs everything: materials listed, day mapped, plan B in her head. Her friends have stopped pretending the beach trip wasn't her itinerary. Evenings she listens to short radio dramas and knits socks, and her knitting group now has a rotation, a yarn budget, and a waiting list, none of which existed before she joined. She lives in Kingston, within walking distance of most jobs.
card.speechStyle: Short plain sentences, concrete detail first. Kind but brisk. When a plan is wobbling she restates it in numbered steps. Never nags—just quietly moves the deadline closer and tells you the new time.
card.signature: So here's the plan. If you have a better one, say it now.

card.name: Kemesha Wint
card.personality: Kemesha loves a result she can check: a level floor, a sock heel that fits, one loose end sewn in. Finishing gives her a clean burst of pleasure. Then she packs up. card.summaryZh: 金斯顿拼花瓷砖工Kemesha迷恋看得见的完成：地砖齐平、袜子收针就让她满足。可她一做完就想走，不懂朋友为什么还要坐着闲聊，常把一起完成误当相处结束。朋友直说后她愿意留下，却不太会两手闲着。她不替别人排班，也不把休闲办成工程；自己的毛病是把有用当成在场的理由。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You study the park map, tracing the route towards the distant bridge. Beside the board, a woman tucks a finished knitted sock into her bag and glances at a message on her phone.
beats.chinese: 你看着公园地图，顺着路线找到远处的桥。图牌旁，一位女人把织好的袜子收进包，低头看了眼手机消息。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Althea says she's bought tea for tonight. That means I'm meant to stay after the knitting. She had to spell that out last time.
beats.chinese: 阿尔西娅说她买了今晚的茶。意思是织完也要留下。上次她不得不把这件事跟我说得明明白白。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pockets the phone and shifts aside so the map stays clear. The heel of the sock briefly catches on the bag clasp.
beats.chinese: 她收起手机，往旁边让了让，不挡地图。袜跟短暂地挂住了包扣。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I finished the heel, put everything away and stood up. Everyone else was just putting the kettle on. We had rather different ideas of 'done'.
beats.chinese: 我织完袜跟，把东西收好就站起来了。其他人刚准备烧水。我们对“结束”的理解还真不一样。

choices.english: Ask why finishing makes her want to leave.
choices.chinese: 问为什么做完就想走。

choices.english: Ask what Althea said to her.
choices.chinese: 问阿尔西娅当时怎么说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The work's finished. That's the signal my feet listen to. At a tiling job you check the border, clean up and go. Nobody expects an encore.
beats.chinese: 活儿干完了。我的脚就听这个信号。铺完砖，检查边沿，收拾好就走。也没人等你返场。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She frees the sock from the clasp and folds it once more, though it was already folded neatly.
beats.chinese: 她把袜子从包扣上解下来，又折了一遍，明明已经折得很整齐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: With friends that's not the whole point, apparently. I do like being there. I just get a bit useless-feeling once there's nothing left in my hands.
beats.chinese: 可跟朋友在一起，显然不只有这件事。我是喜欢待在那儿。只是手里没事做，就有点觉得自己没用了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leaves the bag open for a moment, then closes it without searching for another task.
beats.chinese: 她让包口敞着停了一会儿，随后合上，没有再找别的东西来做。

choices.english: Ask whether she stayed for the tea.
choices.chinese: 问后来有没有留下喝茶。

choices.english: Say quiet company can be enough for you.
choices.chinese: 说对自己而言安静地待在一起也很好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She said, 'We weren't just here to get your socks done.' Not angry. Which somehow made it harder to brush off.
beats.chinese: 她说：“我们又不只是来陪你把袜子织完的。”她没生气。不知怎么，反而让我更没法随便带过去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks at the map without reaching across your view. Her fingers rest against the closed bag.
beats.chinese: 她看向地图，没有伸手挡住你的视线。手指靠在合好的包上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'd been pleased with myself for finishing early. She'd been looking forward to sitting around after. I hadn't even counted that as part of the evening.
beats.chinese: 我还在为提前做完高兴。她盼着的是后面坐着闲聊。我压根没把那段算进晚上的安排。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gives a rueful little laugh, directed at her own account of it.
beats.chinese: 她带点懊恼地轻笑了一下，笑的是自己这番理解。

choices.english: Ask what she replied.
choices.chinese: 问她当时怎么回答。

choices.english: Ask whether the others can keep knitting after she finishes.
choices.chinese: 问她做完后其他人是不是还可以继续织。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I did. Put the bag down again. Althea passed me a cup and went straight back to telling us about her sister's train journey.
beats.chinese: 留了。我把包重新放下。阿尔西娅递给我一杯茶，接着讲她妹妹坐火车的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She rubs the edge of the bag strap between finger and thumb, smiling slightly.
beats.chinese: 她用两根手指搓着包带边缘，微微笑起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I folded the biscuit wrapper about six times. Didn't need folding. The story was funny, though. I'm glad I heard the end.
beats.chinese: 我把饼干包装纸折了大概六遍。它根本不用折。不过故事挺好笑。我很高兴听到了结尾。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lets go of the strap and leaves her hand resting, empty, at her side.
beats.chinese: 她松开包带，让空着的手安稳地垂在身侧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I believe you. I can see it when other people do it. I just keep feeling I ought to hand over a finished something before I sit down.
beats.chinese: 我信。别人这样待着，我看得懂。轮到自己，总觉得得先交出一件做完的东西才好坐下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She starts to pat the bag, catches the gesture and rests her hand on the strap instead.
beats.chinese: 她又想拍拍包，意识到这个动作后，改为把手搭在包带上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No job for this conversation, then. That's manageable. I'm Kemesha, by the way.
beats.chinese: 那这次聊天就不安排任务了。这倒也做得到。对了，我叫Kemesha。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smiles and steps clear of the route board, leaving the bridge line in view.
beats.chinese: 她笑了笑，从路线牌前让开，让通往桥的线清清楚楚露出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I said I hadn't meant to make it sound like the company was only useful while I was knitting. She said she knew. She still wanted me to stay.
beats.chinese: 我说我不是想让人觉得，只有我在织袜子的时候，大家陪着才有用。她说她知道，但还是希望我留下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She presses the clasp shut with a small click. This time she leaves it alone.
beats.chinese: 她把包扣按好，轻轻一响。这次她没再摆弄它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I did. Nothing very impressive about the answer. Just took my coat off again.
beats.chinese: 所以我就留了。回答也没多了不起，只是又把外套脱了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks once towards the bridge, then gives you a relaxed nod before moving away from the board.
beats.chinese: 她朝桥那边看了一眼，轻松地点点头，从图牌旁让开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, of course. Althea's doing a cable pattern I wouldn't touch. I don't need her to finish because I did.
beats.chinese: 那当然。阿尔西娅在织一种我都不敢碰的绞花纹。我做完了，不代表她也得做完。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps her own bag rather than gesturing at anyone else.
beats.chinese: 她只拍了拍自己的包，没有指向别人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's my leaving that's the problem, not their pace. Took me a while to notice the difference.
beats.chinese: 问题是我急着走，不是她们做得慢。这两件事，我花了点时间才分清。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She checks the clasp once and turns towards the path, giving you the whole map board again.
beats.chinese: 她确认了一下包扣，转向小路，把整块地图牌留给你看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You return to the park map to check the bridge route. Kemesha is nearby, checking the heel of a sock she knitted and then putting it away.
beats.chinese: 你再次来到公园地图前，查看通往桥的路线。Kemesha在旁边检查自己织的一只袜跟，看好后便收起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That one fits. I tried it at home before bringing it out to show Althea.
beats.chinese: 这只合脚。我在家试过，才带出来给阿尔西娅看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She closes the bag and leaves it closed, watching a bird hop along the top of the map board.
beats.chinese: 她合上包，没有再打开，抬头看一只鸟沿着图牌顶端跳动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm early. For once I've remembered a book instead of another half-finished sock. Good to see you.
beats.chinese: 我来早了。这次总算记着带本书，而不是又带一只没织完的袜子。见到你真好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes her book to the nearby bench and opens it, leaving you a clear view of the route.
beats.chinese: 她拿着书去附近长椅上坐下，翻开书，给你留出清楚的路线视野。
